projects.title: Vision-Based Collision Safety for the Tumblenauts Swarm
projects.blurb: Keeping a swarm of tiny, randomly tumbling space-inspection robots from colliding
projects.objective: Keep a swarm of small, randomly tumbling inspection robots from colliding in a cramped microgravity space.
projects.approach: A five-camera 3D tracker (audio-synced to within half a frame, AprilTags over 150,000+ frames, SAM 2 segmentation) as the base for a safety filter.
projects.result: In progress. Each robot stays visible to at least one camera 81 to 88% of the time; the fleet flies on a ZeroG parabolic flight in November 2026.
projects.human: Small robots could help watch over the habitats astronauts live in, but only if they can share that space safely.

projects.title: Orbital Data Centers: 1 GW Constellation Analyzer
projects.blurb: Feasibility study and live simulator for a gigawatt-scale data center in space
projects.objective: Find out whether a 1 GW data center could run from orbit.
projects.approach: Led a five-person feasibility study and built a real-time 3D constellation simulator for the orbital architecture.
projects.result: About 20,000 satellites at 550 km make it physically feasible; cost is the binding constraint.
projects.human: AI's demand for power, water, and land is growing faster than the ground can supply it.

projects.title: NANI: AI Medicine Companion
projects.blurb: Built at HackPrinceton Fall 2025: IoT medication adherence for elderly patients
projects.objective: Help an elderly patient take the right medication on time without logging anything.
projects.approach: An IR break-beam pill sensor on a Raspberry Pi, an English and Hindi voice assistant, a cloud pipeline, and a family iOS app.
projects.result: A working end-to-end system built at HackPrinceton Fall 2025.
projects.human: Protects a grandmother's independence and dignity while keeping her family in the loop.

projects.title: Pedestrian Detection Benchmark
projects.blurb: HOG+SVM vs. Faster R-CNN vs. DETR vs. YOLO+SAM2 on hard negatives
projects.objective: Measure how often detectors mistake statues and mannequins for people.
projects.approach: Benchmarked HOG+SVM, Faster R-CNN, DETR, and YOLO+SAM2 on one shared pipeline over the PnPLO dataset.
projects.result: YOLO+SAM2 had the lowest false positive rate and highest mAP; HOG+SVM called almost a third of look-alikes people.
projects.human: A robot that keeps mistaking a mannequin for a person wastes its effort and loses people's trust.

projects.title: Mt. Rainier Railroad Control System
projects.blurb: A closed-loop railroad safety system run by a 6502 computer built from scratch
projects.objective: Detect a fallen tree on the track and protect the train with no human in the loop.
projects.approach: A 6502 computer built from scratch as the supervisor, an Arduino for real-time I/O, and time-of-flight sensors that cut power to a blocked section.
projects.result: A two-loop layout that de-energizes a hazard zone when a tree falls and restores service once the track is clear.
projects.human: Modeled on a real heritage railroad that closed for years after storms brought trees down across its track.

projects.title: RISC-V Processor Simulator
projects.blurb: Functional and cycle-accurate pipelined RV64I simulator with caches
projects.objective: Model a RISC-V processor down to the cycle.
projects.approach: A functional RV64I simulator, extended into a 5-stage pipeline with forwarding, hazard detection, and configurable caches.
projects.result: Cycle-accurate execution validated with 25+ handwritten assembly tests.
projects.human: Knowing where every cycle goes is how software gets faster on real hardware.

projects.title: Autonomous Obstacle-Avoiding Drone
projects.blurb: A CrazyFlie that sees, dodges, and lands on its own
projects.objective: Fly a palm-sized quadrotor through an unknown pillar field to a target and land, with no map and no remote control.
projects.approach: A look, decide, step loop on the onboard Kalman state estimate, with OpenCV color detection for obstacles and the target.
projects.result: Robust runs on demo day; Prof. Nagpal asked to share our code with future classes as an example strategy.
projects.human: Future students in the course now start from a strategy that worked.

projects.title: MATRIX Heliophysics Mission
projects.blurb: Project manager for an 8-spacecraft MIDEX-class constellation design
projects.objective: Design a NASA MIDEX-class mission to study Bursty Bulk Flows in Earth's magnetotail, under a $350M cost cap.
projects.approach: Project manager for 16 people across 8 subsystems, from requirements through a Final Design Review.
projects.result: An eight-spacecraft constellation design, presented to engineers at Johns Hopkins APL.
projects.human: Bursty Bulk Flows drive geomagnetic storms that can disrupt GPS, communications satellites, and radio on the ground.

projects.title: Unwrapping Customer Delight
projects.blurb: Bayesian regression discontinuity for the causal ROI of surprise gifts
projects.objective: Estimate whether surprise gifts actually change what customers spend later.
projects.approach: A Bayesian regression discontinuity design fit with MCMC on 50,000+ anonymized transactions.
projects.result: Credible intervals 15% narrower, with posterior estimates of gift-driven revenue lift.
projects.human: Gives a marketing team a straight answer on whether a campaign is worth its budget.

projects.title: GPU Acceleration of Shap-E on Apple Silicon
projects.blurb: PR to OpenAI's Shap-E: 4+ hours → under 4 minutes
projects.objective: Make OpenAI's Shap-E run on the Apple Silicon GPU instead of falling back to the CPU.
projects.approach: Tracked down the blocking tensor operations and fixed them for PyTorch's MPS backend, keeping CUDA and CPU behavior intact.
projects.result: One image-to-3D generation went from about 4 hours to just under 4 minutes. Pull request filed and awaiting review.
projects.human: If merged, anyone with an Apple Silicon Mac could generate 3D objects locally in minutes.

projects.title: StockSwipe
projects.blurb: Swipe-to-invest stock discovery with Claude-powered analysis
projects.objective: Make stock discovery approachable for people who don't already know what to buy.
projects.approach: A swipe-to-invest card deck with live prices and news, plus Claude-written analysis on the back of every card.
projects.result: A mobile-first app built for the AI@Princeton x Trade[XYZ] Hackathon.
projects.human: Investing apps are built for people who already know what to buy. This one is for everyone else.

projects.title: Genetic Algorithm Orbit Optimizer
projects.blurb: Multi-objective CubeSat orbit design for the Hellenic Space Dawn mission
projects.objective: Optimize CubeSat orbit parameters for the Hellenic Space Dawn mission under coverage, power, and Δv constraints.
projects.approach: A multi-objective genetic algorithm with Pareto front ranking.
projects.result: 30% less computation than exhaustive grid search across 1,000+ scenarios; results went into an ESA-reviewed Design Review.
projects.human: Faster design loops let a small mission team weigh more options before committing to an orbit.

projects.title: NeuroBoost
projects.blurb: A smartwatch concept that estimates cognitive state from wrist biosensors
projects.objective: Estimate cognitive state from sensors a smartwatch already carries.
projects.approach: Paired skin conductance with ECG, PPG, and motion sensing, and designed a machine learning approach to project EEG-like estimates.
projects.result: A seven-person product design with a 3D-printed prototype, a circuit board design, an app, and a clinical trial plan.
projects.human: Everyday help with stress and focus from a watch people already wear, instead of an EEG cap nobody wears to work.

projects.title: ML-Based Fraud Detection
projects.blurb: Kruskal MST clustering with a boosted decision stump
projects.approach: Kruskal MST clustering combined with a boosted decision stump.
projects.result: 98% accuracy on held-out data, tuned for few false negatives.
projects.human: Missed fraud costs people the most, so the threshold favors catching it.

projects.title: Airbnb Price Prediction
projects.objective: Predict New York City Airbnb listing prices.
projects.approach: Feature engineering plus Ridge, Decision Tree, and Random Forest models tuned with GridSearchCV.
projects.result: R² up 9.5% and RMSE down 10%, with Random Forest performing best.
projects.human: Fair price estimates help hosts and travelers know what a listing is worth.

research.title: Multi-Particle Control for Nonlinear Data Assimilation in Chaotic Systems
research.objective: Keep a particle filter locked onto a chaotic system it can only see through noisy observations.
research.approach: An imitation-learning framework that trains a network to imitate an expensive optimal nudging oracle in a single forward pass.
research.result: 77% lower normalized RMSE than the uncontrolled filter on Lorenz-63, scaling to Lorenz-96 with no architectural changes.
research.human: Data assimilation is how forecasts of chaotic systems, like the weather, stay anchored to what is actually happening.

research.title: Learning Particle-Wise Control for Nonlinear Data Assimilation: From Diffusion Models to Supervised Regression
research.objective: Compare diffusion-based and regression-based learned control for particle filtering.
research.approach: A supervised regression framework mapping particle state, observation, and time to observation onto an expert nudging control.
research.result: Found that compatibility with importance sampling, not model power, is the main design constraint.

research.title: Optimal Control in the Filtering of Chaotic Systems Using Adaptive ML Algorithms
research.objective: Lay the groundwork for learned control in particle filters.
research.approach: An HJB-based control formulation, a Lorenz-63 dataset pipeline, and baselines across classical filters.
research.result: The formulation and data pipeline the thesis built on.

patches.name: Princeton Rocketry Club
patches.story: I joined the Rocketry Club my first semester and left it as co-president, after stints as systems engineer, team lead, and professional development officer. As co-president I managed 7 cross-functional project teams across 95+ members, taught new members CAD, flight simulation, composite fabrication, and rocket assembly every semester, and planned a student-led two-stage rocket aimed at suborbital altitude.

patches.name: STAR Lunar Trajectory Team
patches.story: I led a team of 5 interns to find viable lunar trajectory parameters through a trans-lunar injection maneuver. We designed and validated the flight path in GMAT with custom C++ scripts, iterated over launch windows, Δv budgets, and insertion burns, and delivered a feasibility report with recommended mission profiles.

patches.name: MATRIX Mission Team
patches.story: Sixteen people, eight subsystems, one $350M cost cap. I kept the schedule and task tracker, ran the weekly cross-subsystem meetings, and reconciled mass, power, data, and cost margins until the design held together. We took it through a Final Design Review and presented it to engineers at Johns Hopkins APL.

patches.name: Teaching at Princeton
patches.story: Across three semesters of Linear Systems and Intro to Computer Science I have supported 250+ students in office hours and problem sessions, and helped design problem sets and exam questions. The best part is the moment a student says "oh, I get it."
